title: Bump package.json.version by hand in every PR into develop; never expose it in outputs or bump it on promotion
body:
package.json is the ONLY version declaration and nothing consumes it (not /cv.json, /llms.txt or a meta tag). Exposing it would be a contract with no counterpart; add it only when a real consumer exists, and then DERIVE it from package.json at build time, never hand-write a second copy.
Bump at develop because that is where changes enter one at a time; versioning at staging would give a batch one number. develop->staging and staging->main carry the number unchanged, so production shows the version verified in preview.
patch = a fix, nothing reads differently; minor = something new (section, endpoint, datum); major = something existing changes shape (a URL goes away, a /cv.json field renamed).
By hand because patch/minor/major is a semantic call. Rejected: a bot committing the bump (needs a write token on a protected branch and leaves a commit the source lacks -> conflict every merge); deriving from conventional commits (depends on every message being right, adds a dependency). Check before opening the PR: `git fetch origin develop && pnpm run test:version`.
not_derivable: The rejected automation options, the bump semantics and the 'do not expose' rule are not in code.

evidence.summary: Gate: PR version strictly greater than develop's.
